title: Bounded PDF/HTML reference navigation
summary: Use this whenever a sphere points at a PDF/HTML manual. The normal cycle is find or locate -> read the returned physical page/HTML section -> move -1/+1/+N/-N for surrounding context -> return to the originating article/task.
invariants: PDF physical page number and printed/manual page label are different identities.
A printed-page lookup is approximate until the returned physical page is inspected.
Find returns bounded excerpts and an exact physical-page/section selector; it does not dump the whole document.
URL fetching is bounded by byte limit and temporary; the response records resolved source, byte size and SHA-256.
Previous/next/+N/-N navigation operates on physical PDF pages or bounded HTML sections.
Text extraction is evidence access, not authority over the source document's interpretation.
procedure: Use `reference find` when you know a phrase.
Use `reference locate --reference-page N --approx-page M` when a citation refers to printed page N but front matter makes physical PDF page uncertain.
Use `reference read` on the returned location.
Use `reference move ... +1/-1/+5/-5` to inspect surrounding pages.
Return to the originating sphere/article once the bounded primary evidence has been read.
